$comment: The single source of truth for every public accessibility claim: the target, the conformance report, the tested screen readers and browsers, the known limitations, and the notes. Shape, consumers, and how to change it: docs/AGENTS.md, section 2.20. Docs pages read it through {{$a11y.<key>}} template variables, the READMEs and the website read the strings it renders, and scripts/accessibility-claims.mjs fails on any public text that contradicts it.

wording.long: targets WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA

audit.coverage: the Level A and AA criteria its tables mark as evaluated; of the six criteria new in WCAG 2.2 (2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, and 3.3.8), four were judged internally and two (2.4.11 and 2.5.8) are not evaluated yet

next.scope: every Level A and AA criterion judged, the evaluated product version stated, and the international edition of the VPAT template

knownLimitations.text: Sorting state changes are not announced to screen readers.
A range selection is not announced; only the focused cell is.
Nested column headers are not announced reliably.
There is no option to give the grid an accessible description.
A cell that shows a formula result is not distinguished from a typed value.
The position of an empty cell is not announced.
The date picker (Pikaday) is not announced properly.
The loading icon (an SVG) is not hidden from screen readers.
The dialog's default accessible name is the word "Dialog"; pass `a11y.ariaLabel` in the dialog settings to name it after its content.
Menu separators are exposed as interactive menu items.
The checkboxes in the filter menu are labeled "Checked" or "Unchecked" instead of with the value they stand for.
The summary row and some icons of the Horizon theme fail the contrast ratio.
With frozen rows, frozen columns, or both, some screen readers read the total number of rows and columns incorrectly.
When you select a cell in a frozen row or column, NVDA might announce the wrong column header name.
Screen readers sometimes omit ARIA attributes that change dynamically.

The `aria-rowcount` attribute is set to `-1` on purpose, because most screen readers ignore or misread it; this keeps VoiceOver accurate. Handsontable revisits this when screen readers handle the attribute consistently.

notes.mobile: VoiceOver on iOS was part of the last audit. Mobile screen readers are checked by hand once per major release.
notes.automation: Screen-reader checks are manual today. The automated nightly runs with NVDA and VoiceOver that are being set up join this list when they run.
